what: membership inference against the training procedure, over shadow models
data: LIDC-IDRI (TCIA, CC BY 3.0): the 1,178 labelled 28 mm crops of the 518 training patients of docs/measurements/medical-nodule3d-split.json; the validation part selects every model's epoch, as in training; the test part is not touched

teacher.name: resnet3d18
teacher.held_fixed: every shadow distils from the real run's out-of-fold probabilities, each computed by a teacher fold that did not see that crop but saw the other training patients, shadow members and non-members alike

label: the readers' label (median malignancy rating), on which every model is scored

models.control: the control arm: conv 1->4 (3x3x3), batch norm, ReLU, avg-pool 2, dense 4*14^3 -> 2
models.square: the shipped arm: conv 1->4 (3x3x3), batch norm, x^2, avg-pool 2, dense 4*14^3 -> 2

design.membership: complementary pairs: each record a member of exactly half the models

attacks.lira_online: Carlini et al., IEEE S&P 2022 (arXiv:2112.03570); implemented here
attacks.rmia_offline: Zarifzadeh, Liu and Shokri, ICML 2024 (arXiv:2312.03262); implemented here and checked against ML Privacy Meter's run_rmia at e384af8fd931

not_resolvable: fpr 0.001: 0.0056 of non-members tie at the top score
fpr 0.001: 0.0062 of non-members tie at the top score

reading: TPR at a fixed low FPR is the measure; an AUC near 0.5 with TPR near the FPR means the attack learns little about membership from this model's outputs. An attack gives a lower bound on leakage, not a proof of its absence.
